Definition: from G1487 and G3361; if not:--but, except (that), if not, more than, save (only) that, saving, till.
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means if not, but, or except, and it is one of the commonest turns in the Gospels, always made of if and not standing side by side. Salt is good for nothing except to be cast out, no one knows the Father except the Son, and David ate the showbread, which was not lawful for him to eat except for the priests alone. The phrase marks the one door through which the rule opens.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe except is the word that keeps God's rules from becoming traps, because He always names the way through.
